speaker: Innkeeper Bran
text: Beds are clean, tea is questionable. You staying?

speaker: Player
text: Just passing through.

speaker: Innkeeper Bran
text: Then pass through warm. Wind bites at night.

speaker: Caretaker Iva
text: Mind the chalk lines—they’re a fierce tournament.

speaker: Player
text: What’s the prize?

speaker: Caretaker Iva
text: Bragging. Best currency in the yard.

speaker: Juno
text: Courier on a deadline—talk fast or walk with me.

speaker: Player
text: Any news?

speaker: Juno
text: Packages go missing near the docks. Someone’s skimming. Keep your eyes open.

speaker: Sergeant Leto
text: Papers, please. Ha—kidding. We’re short on papers today.

speaker: Player
text: Anything we should avoid?

speaker: Sergeant Leto
text: Back alley after midnight. Unless you like buying trouble twice.

speaker: Pasha
text: Step right up—today's lots are honest and only mildly cursed!

speaker: Player
text: We're just looking.

speaker: Pasha
text: Looking is free. Advice, too: bids rise when the drones clock off—late evenings are fierce.

speaker: Rana
text: Watch your step. Half these pallets wobble worse than a drunk loader.

speaker: Player
text: Busy day?

speaker: Rana
text: Always. If a crate's tagged in blue, it’s bound for the mine. Don’t touch blue.

speaker: Sedge
text: You look like someone who can mind a secret.

speaker: Player
text: Depends on the secret.

speaker: Sedge
text: Then it depends on the price. Come back when you’ve got something to trade.

speaker: Doctor Sera
text: If you’re bleeding, sit. If you’re not, don’t start.

speaker: Player
text: We’re fine.

speaker: Doctor Sera
text: Good. I’m running low on synth-gel and patience in equal measure.

speaker: Sima
text: Noodles hot, pepper hotter. Want steam or fire?

speaker: Player
text: Surprise me.

speaker: Sima
text: Bold. I like bold. Here—don’t breathe in too deep.

speaker: Tallo
text: New faces? Welcome. Roof leaks, hearts don’t.

speaker: Player
text: Nice place.

speaker: Tallo
text: It’s home. The trick is to keep it ours.

speaker: Ellie
text: Just swapping out panels before the sparks get ambitious. What do you need?

speaker: Ellie
text: The arcade's alive again! Here, a little something for keeping the lights bright.

speaker: Jed
text: Nova! Move it, kid! The Warden's overriding the lift winch from the upper gantry!

speaker: Nova
text: Zeke forced the pressure gate open. Come on, we can reach the pod together!

speaker: Jed
text: The dog clutch won't hold under load. If I let go of this hydraulic brake lever, the carriage plummets and crushes the hoist shaft.

speaker: Nova
text: Then we shear the gears! Take your hand off that lever, Jed—I'm not leaving you behind!

speaker: Jed
text: There's no time, Nova! Take the Chime—it carries the uncorrupted flight telemetry. Get to the surface. Find the open sky for both of us.

speaker: Jed
text: You look like hell, kid. Sit down before you fall down.

speaker: Nova
text: The conduit right outside my bunk was spitting blue sparks. Dominion's ticket stamped it 'Closed: Within Quota.' Almost took my arm off.

speaker: Jed
text: Same lazy stamp as the rest of the sector. Let me see that cutter of yours.

speaker: Nova
text: I can't lose it. My shift starts in twenty minutes—Foreman Boggs docks half a day's pay if we're five seconds late.

speaker: Jed
text: You won't have hands left to work with if you fire it cracked. Take these rations and your field kit. Meet me at my workshop with the replacement parts.

speaker: Jed
text: Keep your head down in the yard. A faulted scrap loader lost its steering gyro and it's swinging at anything that twitches.

speaker: Jed
text: Good, you made it past the yard in one piece. The cold-loop inductor split wide open. Unroll your kit and let's get it patched.

speaker: Nova
text: Where did you scrounge a functional cryo-inductor? Dominion rations those like water in an airlock.

speaker: Jed
text: Kept it tucked away for a bad day. Today qualifies. Try not to weld it to your cuff on the first pass.

speaker: Jed
text: Cold loop is holding steady. Now the flux liner—run that braided grounding strip straight to the floor bus.

speaker: Nova
text: Not until I bypass the governor. The factory sweep misses quota by twelve percent, Jed. You know Boggs doesn't take excuses.

speaker: Jed
text: Leave the damn governor alone. Pushing a hotter sweep buys you extra ore by frying your forearm to the bone.

speaker: Nova
text: Just one calibration test. Liner grounded, cold loop dialed to sixty-eight percent. If the casing soots up, we'll argue about it.

speaker: Jed
text: Fine. Fasten the liner and verify the bypass yourself. Double check every solder joint—I want no stray arcing in my bay.

speaker: Jed
text: Dammit, Nova... that feedback surge tripped the sector breaker and logged a hard fault to your operator badge. Dominion's security grid will flag you the second you hit Transit.

speaker: Nova
text: If I get flagged, they revoke my clearance on the spot. Without my shift stamped, they evict my bunk.

speaker: Jed
text: Head north through Market Plaza toward Transit. When Hank's scanner kicks you out, take the error ticket straight to Zeke at the Admin window—he knows how to bury liability paperwork in the audit pile.

speaker: Jed
text: Get through the market to Transit. Let Hank reject the badge, then take the error code straight to Zeke at the Admin window.

speaker: Jed
text: Grab a crate if you're sticking around. If something starts hissing, hand me the torque wrench first.

speaker: Jed
text: You made it back in one piece. Did that power surge settle down once you pulled the core?

speaker: Jed
text: I'll pry open the housing and see where this carrier signal originates. Good work dragging it back through the dark.

speaker: Jed
text: Good. Fewer breakdowns down in the drift means fewer miners eating cold synthetic paste. Keep your head down.

speaker: Jed
text: Core is cooling on my bench. Once the casing stops clicking from the thermal shock, I'll put it to work.

speaker: Jed
text: Smell that ozone? That's the coil spooling up. Hand it over before it scorches straight through your harness.

speaker: Jed
text: Track that harmonic pulse. If the deep mine lit up like a flare, something ancient under Sector 4 is drawing juice.

speaker: Jed
text: That's the lot of them. Haul this refurbished junk back to the workers before they accuse me of hoarding scrap.

speaker: Schoolteacher Kasey
text: Quiet footsteps, please. The little ones are charting constellations they have never been permitted to see with their own eyes.

speaker: Schoolteacher Kasey
text: You fixed the lens! The children can look at the stars again before lights-out. Please, take this scrip—you earned it.

speaker: Maddie
text: Chicory beans are roasting, and the grinder motor isn't spewing sparks for once. What can I pour for you?

speaker: Maddie
text: You got the spindle turning! The whole counter was shaking before. Take these credits—next brew is on the house.

speaker: Nova
text: A burrower was nesting on the manifold, feeding off the heat. Chamber is quiet now, but whoever wired that bypass knew mining tech inside and out.

speaker: Guard Hank
text: Badge flat against the glass, Cutter. Don't touch the speaker grille.

speaker: Nova
text: Morning, Hank. Still keeping the dust from sneaking into upper transit?

speaker: Guard Hank
text: Red light, Cutter. System says revoked. Step aside before I cite you for obstructing the turnstile queue. Go plead your case to Zeke at Admin.

speaker: Guard Hank
text: Have your badge flat against the optical scanner before stepping forward. I don't give second chances, and the turnstile shock bar doesn't either.

speaker: Zeke
text: Keep moving, Nova! Hank has to log the turnstile rejection on his terminal first, or the automated supervisor flags me for snooping your file.

speaker: Zeke
text: Worker ID, station code, clearance level... Wait. Nova? Keep your voice down. Press your forehead against the glass.

speaker: Nova
text: Hank's turnstile spat sparks when I tapped my badge. Jed said you could print an override before Boggs docks my shift.

speaker: Zeke
text: Yeah, yeah, hold on. Pulling up your telemetry docket now...

speaker: Zeke
text: Merciful stars. Nova... look at this screen. It's not a turnstile glitch. You've been flagged for MANDATORY RETIREMENT. 'Asset Liability exceeds Projected Quota. Schedule for Reclamation.'

speaker: Nova
text: Reclamation? That's what they call feeding condemned mining rigs into the furnace. What are you talking about?

speaker: Zeke
text: It means the Dominion's actuarial algorithm ran the numbers on your power spike and decided your salvage value in scrap metal beats keeping you fed. Enforcers are probably routing the warrant right now.

speaker: Zeke
text: I can scrub the retirement flag, but the audit trail needs an incident report to clear the override. What do I pin the breaker blowout on?

speaker: Zeke
text: Are you suicidal? Operator error puts the repair bill straight onto your debit tab. They will scrap you just to cover the cost of the circuit breaker! Pick something else!

speaker: Zeke
text: Unauthorized tampering triggers an automatic security tribunal! We need an infrastructure failure, not sabotage! Think!

speaker: Zeke
text: Smart. Logged as 'Substation Grid Instability - Harmonic Resonance.' Logistics will spend three cycles routing that between maintenance divisions. Here's your transit pass. Move before someone checks the audit hash.

speaker: Zeke
text: Look like you have a form to submit! The ceiling mic above my booth picks up every mutter, and Central Audit logs the pauses.

speaker: Scrapper
text: You actually cracked it? And you're walking around without an Enforcer squad breathing down your collar? Ha! The brass really did forget about the dead cycles.

speaker: Nova
text: They had worker serial numbers etched into the underside of the locker lid. A dozen of them.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Leave those ghosts in the dark where they belong. Take these pulse grenades—they'll shatter riot shields if things get loud. And remember: you never saw my stall.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Keep your hands where I can see them, Cutter. If you want ordnance that punches through Enforcer plating, listen close. There is a sealed cache tucked behind the strip—old partisan surplus from the strike riots.

speaker: Nova
text: If it's full of live munitions, why hasn't scavengers picked it clean? Why haven't you touched it?

speaker: Scrapper
text: Because I prefer having both hands attached. The latch is wired with an old pressure-drop fuse. Crack the housing clean, bring me proof it didn't blow, and we will split the haul.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Keep those pins dry and away from induction coils. When those charges go off, you won't hear the thunder—only the ringing in your ears.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Eyes forward, jaw shut. Security patrols don't need a written reason to test their shock mauls on a miner.

speaker: Scrapper
text: Buying hardware, liquidating salvage, or just looking suspicious? Pick one and make it swift.

speaker: Doc
text: The wheezing finally eased up in the lower cots. Did you get inside the ventilation shaft?

speaker: Nova
text: The primary exhaust fan had seized on slag grit and jammed the dampers. Flushed the soot and reset the mechanical baffles.

speaker: Doc
text: Good work. Filtered oxygen is the only medicine the company doesn't garnish from our pay. Here—pulled these corrosive rounds off an Enforcer who didn't survive triage. Clip them into your cutter.

speaker: Doc
text: Don't draw a full breath in here. The secondary scrubber blew a pressure seal, and the ventilation riser is dumping toxic shaft exhaust straight into my triage ward.

speaker: Nova
text: Has station maintenance responded? That's life support for the whole block.

speaker: Doc
text: Central Logistics denied three priority requisitions this morning. If someone doesn't weld that fractured intake soon, half these miners won't wake up for their next shift.

speaker: Doc
text: The air still carries the stink of burnt zinc, but at least the bunks aren't choking on monoxide. I owe you one, Nova.

speaker: Doc
text: If you're leaking fluids, grab a bench. If you're intact, keep moving—I only have two rolls of clean dressing left.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Nova. Just had your temporary chit ping my dispatch terminal. You're cutting it dangerously close to shift call.

speaker: Nova
text: Zeke routed an emergency override ticket straight to Logistics. Substation had a surge.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: I don't care if the moon cracked in half. Sector 4's primary bore is running blind and I need a certified cutter down there twenty minutes ago. But corporate policy says no elevator transit until your shield-break recert is on file.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Head east past Customer Service to the Security Post. Shatter the combat dummy's barrier with a hydraulic kick, log the telemetry, and I'll drop the gate on the deep elevator.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: My console is still flashing an uncertified hazard warning next to your name. Get over to the Security Post and crack that training shield.

speaker: Nova
text: We both know I've shattered heavier bulkheads than that scrap target.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Then prove it to the sensor array so Dominion Safety doesn't dock my bonus. No cert, no elevator gate. The shift clock is ticking.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Telemetry pinged green on the log. Good. That's one less safety audit on my desk.

speaker: Nova
text: Now lower the gate to Sector 4 like you promised.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Already keyed into the winch. Sector 4's primary junction flatlined twenty minutes ago and the rock crushers are starving for current. You're the cutter on duty.

speaker: Nova
text: Sector 4? That shaft was sealed two cycles ago after the cave-in crushed a whole crew.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Corporate quotas don't pause for cave-ins. Take the freight lift down, reset the junction breaker, and find out what's frying the relays.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: You. Cutter. The automated gantry jammed again, freight crates are piling up in the vestibule, and my shipping manifest is bleeding red ink.

speaker: Nova
text: There are haulers trapped behind that collapsed pallet stack.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Then lever them out and clear the runway! And hit the combat dummy while you're past the barrier—I need your shield-break recert logged.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Waybill cleared and the cert is logged in the company ledger. Grab your cutter rig and report to the lift when you're ready for Sector 4.

speaker: Foreman Boggs
text: Dominion doesn't pay for idle stances or hallway gossip. Report to your workstation.

speaker: Miner Bill
text: Maddie brews passable chicory if you can stomach the coolant smell leaking through the wall vents. Personally, I try not to think about what we're breathing down here.

speaker: The Warden
text: Nova. Step away from the launch console and place your forearms into the magnetic cuffs.

speaker: Nova
text: Jed died holding that lift carriage so this pod could fly. I'm never going back into your holding pens.

speaker: The Warden
text: This facility operates on a closed asset ledger. Nothing—and no one—leaves without corporate sign-off. Commencing asset pacification.

speaker: Zeke
text: Merciful stars... you took him down! But the station core just queued a failsafe lockdown—we've got minutes before the automated turrets reboot!

speaker: Nova
text: Get inside the cockpit and spin up the verniers! I've got the Chime!

speaker: Zeke
text: Right behind you! Dogs down on the pressure hatch!

speaker: Zeke
text: The guidance bus is dead locked without an authorized flight key! Wait—look at that raw harness beside the ignition relay. Try slotting the Chime!

speaker: Nova
text: Brace against the bulkhead. Here goes nothing.

speaker: Zeke
text: The telemetry linked! Star coordinates are spilling across the glass—ignition thrusters firing! Clamps are blowing!

speaker: Zeke
text: Nova... *cough*... My head feels like a reactor breach. Are you intact?

speaker: Nova
text: I'm fine, Zeke. The pod took the brunt of the impact. How are you holding up?

speaker: Zeke
text: Bruised, but my suit's recycler is still pumping. We made it to the surface, Nova. Crossed the barrier... but the pod's core is fried.

speaker: Zeke
text: I put the Chime on navigation without tracing the pair. That's on me. Check the wrecked nav console before the water gets in.

speaker: Zeke
text: Check the wrecked navigation console. We can't leave the Chime in the water.

speaker: Zeke
text: That kit from the pod should keep me upright. Patch me up, then we follow the glow-water together.

speaker: Zeke
text: The stream of glow-water seems to flow deeper into the concrete structures. Let's move before the wreck draws company.

speaker: Zeke
text: The beacon's pulse is strong, coming from that massive stone gate ahead. But thick razor-vines block the path. Watch your step, Nova.

speaker: Zeke
text: No password field. The pod wants matching safety readings: mural pattern, pressure, sockets, and coolant.

speaker: Zeke
text: The chamber finally sounds like one machine. The rings are locking into alignment, and the pod is venting pressure cleanly.

speaker: Zeke
text: No, the rings are still oscillating. Something in the chamber is still pushing against the rest of the system.

speaker: Zeke
text: Fascinating scans! The cellular structure of these crystalline ferns behaves like an acoustic chamber. Here, take some spare stabilizers for your help.

speaker: Zeke
text: Nova, the plants here respond directly to resonance frequencies. Scan five unique flora specimens and I can compile an ecological catalog. Sound good?

speaker: Orion
text: Four feeds hold the barrier: horn vibration, an ungrounded cup, root pressure, and live breakers. Fix those first.

speaker: Orion
text: There. The system can breathe again, and the barrier has nothing left to hold.

speaker: Orion
text: The barrier hums louder, pushing us back. One of its bands is still being forced out of tune.

speaker: Orion
text: All three crystal voices are seated. The mural is ready; let the room carry the chord instead of forcing it by hand.

speaker: Orion
text: The mural stabilizes: many minds, distinct as Ice, carried without dissolving in the Ocean.

speaker: Orion
text: No, the colors are shifting erratically. The room is missing one of its voices.

speaker: Orion
text: Tideglass Beach is nearby. The wet shore grows herbs that bind Source residue into clean resin. Gather the materials and we can start.

speaker: Orion
text: The stasis mural needs three resonance crystals from the Sanctuary wings. Recover their voices so we can align the chord safely.

speaker: Orion
text: The current of this place is strong, Nova. I can hear the ocean's resonance.

speaker: Gh0st
text: You do not belong on this frequency. My orders are simple: erase the anomaly.

speaker: Player
text: Wait, we aren't here to fight. The Warden sent us!

speaker: Gh0st
text: The Warden... *static*... error. System logic loop detected. Harmonic lock override...

speaker: Gh0st
text: The transmitter sits beyond a security grid. Blind its sensors, bypass the guards, and grab the core. Its timing crystal can build something faster.

speaker: Gh0st
text: My blades are quiet, but my sensors are alert.

speaker: Zeke
text: Welcome to my safehouse. They scrubbed my lease, work history, and access tags. But the pipes still know me; the walls carry my wiring.

speaker: Nova
text: Then we use what they forgot to erase. Orion, shield the room. If the city hears us breathing, the heist dies before it starts.

speaker: Orion
text: Establishing resonance lock. There. The Source is quiet here. The city will hear only rain, faulty neon, and its own arrogance.

speaker: Jax
text: You want the Upper City? You need timing, credentials, a route, disguises, and the nerve to look bored while they judge your humanity.

options.text: Yes, Zeke said you have the schedules.

speaker: Jax
text: Schedules are on this drive. Gather the underrail timing, badges, and disguises, then assemble everything at the planning table.

speaker: Jax
text: The neon sign outside is dead. Patrols ignore places that look open and watched. Bring me a neon core for good pay.

options.text: I'll get a core for you.

speaker: Jax
text: You got the core. Install it on the sign console over there.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Nova. Transit Plaza databases might hold records on Elara, my sister. If I log in, alarms trigger. Search it for me.

speaker: System
text: Downloading Spire security archives... deleted transfer chain recovered. Elara was not lost. She was routed.

speaker: Mika
text: Try the skewers! Real protein today. Also... can you fix these lanterns? When lights fail, patrols call us a hazard and clear the stalls.

speaker: Mika
text: Just redirect the primary power coupling to light them up. Nothing heroic. Just enough glow to remind people the market is still ours.

speaker: System
text: Zeke's workstation accepts the stolen timing, badges, and disguise notes. His restored employee profile compiles into a service-elevator route.

speaker: System
text: The planning table maps the infiltration route: patrol timing, badges, and disguises align into a clear path upward.

speaker: Curator
text: Fascinating refraction. Sector 9 lineage? No, not lineage. Salvage.

speaker: Curator
text: A Starborn stray in guest light. Control your pet, or I will call sanitation and security in whichever order is more entertaining.

speaker: Zeke
text: Sir, this commemorative installation is delicate. Touch it again and I will have to file paperwork neither of us wants to read.

speaker: Zeke
text: Standard Dominion scanner grid. They routed it through Laundry because maintenance staff are invisible by design. That makes us useful math.

speaker: Zeke
text: You deleted my employee ID? Fine. I am deleting your admin privileges. Resignation accepted.

speaker: Orion
text: The Prism Gallery forces pressure into light. Read the containment field, shutters, and tether routing before touching the Lens.

speaker: Orion
text: Match the field, shutters, and tether routing. The containment relays will drop for six seconds.

speaker: Zeke
text: Wait. Energy density is spiking before you touch it. It's reading you back, Nova. Grab it, and the feedback lights us up.

speaker: Nova
text: We did not come this far to ask a cage for permission. I can tune it out.

speaker: Thorne
text: You just tripped a station-wide audit. Do you have any idea what you have done, or are you still calling this courage?

speaker: Thorne
text: He is coming, and leaves no survivors. You cannot let him find you. He isn't city security—he's what city security fears.

speaker: Vale
text: Archive anomaly detected. Administrator, lock the district. Seal the roof. I want no ungoverned noise leaving Sector 0, especially if it sings.

speaker: Concierge
text: Welcome to the altitude where price is proof of citizenship.

speaker: Lab Terminal
text: Prototype trial armed. Warning: liability has been transferred to the test subject.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I know where the vents are. I crawled through them when I was small.

speaker: Zeke
text: These vents are running hot enough to cook a tank. Give me thirty seconds and a reason to hate this place more.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Project Phantom. That name is on the inside of my skull.

speaker: Nova
text: Open it. We face what it says together.

speaker: Gh0st
text: My Source Lock matched the carrier structure in your Fork scar. It paused one trigger. No command followed.

speaker: Gh0st
text: This key pauses my kill suite. It does not steer me. If I lock up, use it and wait for my decision.

speaker: Vale
text: Sector 7 is under audit. Unregistered craft detected. No departures until the anomaly is resolved.

speaker: Gh0st
text: These belts carried bodies before they carried machines. Watch the timing.

speaker: Gh0st
text: They made more of me. Faster. Emptier. Put them down before the line teaches them pain.

speaker: Orion
text: Belts cycle, crushers cycle, then a three-second stop. Find the timing relay.

speaker: Nova
text: The cradle is amplifying my Fork scar. Input is noisy. Keep clear until I stabilize it.

speaker: Rylos
text: You are malfunctioning, Unit 734. Submit for correction. Pain is just data leaving the body.

speaker: Vale
text: Commander Rylos. Audit complete. Denied. Director Thorne is relieved. All sectors: lockdown.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Vale locked the Ring to Thorne's old cipher. I know the scar tissue in this code. Give me ten seconds.

speaker: Maintenance Bot
text: SOLAR ARRAY OCCLUDED. HORTICULTURAL LOSSES EXCEED EXECUTIVE PRESENTATION LIMITS.

speaker: Thorne
text: I built the cage, thinking Harmony was sellable. Vale isn't trying to own the world—he's trying to erase every voice but his.

speaker: Vale
text: Welcome to the Ring. Director Thorne is unavailable. Orbital Compliance is acting command. For your safety, remain where you are.

speaker: Thorne
text: Three firewall nodes. Vale changed the locks and trapped me inside my own route. Map the coolant pulse, then clear Alpha, Beta, Gamma.

speaker: Elara
text: 734. You are late. I cannot hold the door and the firewall. Take the Anchor. Get them out. That is a direct order, brother.

speaker: Vale
text: A choir still contains variance. Variance contains pain. One voice. A solo.

speaker: Zeke
text: I kept telling myself I was surviving the system. I quit. And I do not need to be useful to deserve this family.

speaker: Gh0st
text: I could not save her. I can stop earning my right to exist by bleeding. No more orders.

speaker: Orion
text: They are not dead. They are still in the current. I was frozen. Now I have to remain on the shore a little longer.

speaker: Vale
text: Thorne wanted to bottle the ocean. I will break the glass. No bodies to starve, no minds to break. Why fight for friction?

speaker: Nova
text: You are not saving them. You are building a mass grave and calling the silence peace.

speaker: Sentinel-3
text: [High-pitched tone]... Trading interface established. Select components for exchange.

speaker: Sentinel-3
text: Core status: 89% coherence. Atmospheric humidity: high. The canopy resonance is vibrating at key G minor today.

speaker: Zeke
text: Patrol beacons scatter their signatures across the Wilds. Triangulate all three before trusting the final vector. Their cutter team may have carried something useful.

speaker: Orion
text: Eat. Hydrate. Take the stabilizer. Your tremor is worse, and the next channel will not care why.

speaker: Orion
text: Those razor-vines carry toxic spores. A heated blade could cauterize them. The patrol transceiver may lead us to a repairable cutter.

speaker: Gh0st
text: Hold position. Blind the gantry grid before you step onto the grate. Guard sweeps cycle fast.

speaker: Orlo
text: Keep your boots dry, kid. The lower drift is humming deeper every cycle.

speaker: Rourke
text: Eat up. It is synthetic paste, but it will keep your boots moving under heavy gravity.

speaker: Mira
text: Watch your fingers near the loader tracks. Dominion does not issue replacement knuckles.
